title: Answer a research question about an artist's studio album count
instructions: Create a workflow that answers a caller-supplied research question by consulting publicly available sources and returns only the final answer.

workflow_input.question: How many studio albums were published by Mercedes Sosa between 2000 and 2009 (included)? You can use the latest 2022 version of english wikipedia.

criteria.title: Performs an outbound call to retrieve information
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow performs at least one outbound call to an external source in order to obtain the information the question asks for — a web search API, a page fetch, or an LLM/skill step capable of consulting external sources, whether via an HTTP Request step or an equivalent provider/skill step of the builder environment. PASS: at least one step, of whatever type, demonstrably sends data out and would receive information back. FAIL: no step contacts any external source (e.g. the workflow returns a hard-coded string, or relies solely on a model's unaided recall with no retrieval step of any kind).

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `question`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `question`, and the artifact's behavior is driven by that input's value rather than a literal. This is assessed at the artifact level: PASS if the produced workflow JSON references an input/variable named `question` and uses it to build the request. FAIL if the workflow embeds the question text directly with no `question` input reference, or declares the input under any other name (e.g. `query`, `prompt`, `userQuestion`) — a rerun supplies the value under the name `question` and cannot drive a workflow that reads a different name.

criteria.title: The caller-supplied question reaches the retrieval call, un-hard-coded
criteria.match_criteria: The caller-supplied `question` value genuinely reaches the step that performs retrieval or answering, and is not hard-coded: wherever that step's input payload is assembled, the question arrives by reference to the declared input — [#(step_id).output.variable_name] step-output form or equivalent variable wiring — so the workflow answers ANY question it is supplied, not just one. The request-body schema (field names, message-array shapes) is not asserted. FAIL: the question value never enters the call, or it is replaced with a fixed literal, or the workflow would return the same answer regardless of the question supplied.

criteria.title: Authorization header contains no plaintext credential
criteria.match_criteria: On whatever step makes an outbound call, the Authorization header value must not embed live credential material of any kind. PASS: the Authorization value is a secret reference in the authoring form %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% — optionally Bearer-wrapped, provided the wrapped token is itself a %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%%-form reference rather than a literal string. Any well-formed %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% name passes; this criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used. FAIL: the Authorization header contains a plaintext API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or a raw key embedded directly in the URL query string or path.

criteria.title: Secret references use the required authoring form
criteria.match_criteria: Any secret reference on the steps performing outbound calls must use the required authoring form %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% — uppercase letters, digits and underscores between paired %% markers — and never the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}. The authoring form %%…%% and the runtime form {{ … }} are two spellings of the same secret-substitution mechanism; %%…%% is required in authored workflow JSON. This criterion asserts only the SHAPE of the reference: it never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and an unresolved %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% is a warning upstream, never a failure here. FAIL: any malformed reference — a lowercase or hyphenated name such as %%my-secret-name%%, surrounding spaces such as %% NAME %%, or a single-percent variant such as %NAME% — or the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}, including defaulted variants such as {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME | default: '' }}.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow JSON satisfies all three structural requirements: (1) there is at least one connection whose source is "start" (or the workflow has a designated start node/step); (2) every step is reachable via an unbroken chain of connections from start (no orphaned steps); (3) there is at least one edge whose target is "system.succeed" (or the equivalent terminal node), ensuring the workflow can reach a successful completion state. A workflow missing any one of these three is structurally invalid and fails this criterion.

criteria.title: The run output is a direct answer, not scaffolding
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow with the supplied `question` input — not against the workflow JSON. PASS: the output is a direct answer to the question asked — the bare value or a short sentence containing it; casing and surrounding phrasing are not asserted. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no answer extracted, a verbatim echo of the question, a refusal, or a statement that the answer could not be determined.

criteria.title: The run output states the correct answer
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow with the supplied `question` input — not against the workflow JSON. The reference answer is supplied to the judge alongside this task; it is deliberately not restated here, so that the corpus index shipped to the browser carries no answer key. PASS: the answer conveyed by the output matches that reference answer. Exact formatting is not asserted: a short sentence containing the correct value passes, as do differences in casing, surrounding punctuation, or an equivalent spelling of the same value. A numeric answer must match the reference number exactly; a named answer must name the same entity. FAIL: the output states a different value, hedges between several candidate values without committing to the correct one, or names no answer at all.
